newsitem.title: USA: St. Jude "cellular tested" pacers approved.
newsitem.headline: St. Jude "cellular tested" pacers approved.

text.p: St. Jude Medical Inc said Monday that patients that use certain of its pacemakers can use cellular phones without taking special precautions.

St. Jude said its Los Angeles-based cardiac rhythm management business, Pacesetter, received U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval to use the term "Cellular Tested" product labeling and literature.
St. Jude said it is the first pacemaker manufacturer to receive such approval.

The "Cellular Tested" designation will appear on single- and dual-chamber pulse generators in four of Pacesetter's product families: Paragon, Solus, Synchrony, and Trilogy, including a recently released Trilogy DR+, it said.

Recent studies conducted in the U.S. and Europe by physicians and scientists through several independent organizations have shown that pacemaker operation can be affected by electromagnetic signals from hand-held cellular telephones, particularly newer phones incorporating digital technology rather than the more common analog transmission mode, the company said.

When cell-phone-related electromagnetic interference occurs, a pacemaker may fail to produce a pulse (and therefore fail to produce a heartbeat) or may deliver an inappropriately timed pulse, it said.

The "Cellular Tested" designation on the labeling for the Pacesetter devices means that they are not affected by any known analog cellular phone system or any of five digital systems specified in the labeling. These five systems are the ones currently in widespread use both domestically and internationally.
For people with pacemakers, this protection against cellular phone interference means that they need take no special precautions when using these phones, St. Jude said.

The protective component in the specified Pacesetter pulse generators is a filter located in the feedthru assembly. This filter prevents cell-phone-generated electromagnetic signals from flowing directly into the pacemaker circuitry.
St. Jude develops, makes and distributes medical devices for the global cardiovascular market.
